items.content:
최첨단 AI 모델들이 실제 기업의 전문 업무를 재현한 평가에서 최고 12%에 그쳤습니다. 기존 벤치마크가 실제 업무의 복잡성과 전문가의 판단 과정을 충분히 반영하지 못한다는 지적과 함께, AI가 기업의 고부가가치 전문 업무를 얼마나 완수할 수 있는지 측정하는 새로운 평가 방식이 등장했습니다.

반도체·AI 산업 분석 전문 세미애널리시스(SemiAnalysis)는 2일(현지시간) 새로운 AI 에이전트 벤치마크인 ' GDPx '를 공개했습니다. 반도체 설계, 사이버보안, 생물학, 금융, 법률, 소프트웨어 개발, AI 자기 개선(RSI) 등 11개 전문 분야에서 206개 작업을 수행하도록 했습니다. 이를 위해 전문 업체 14곳과 협력해 실제 업무 환경을 재현했습니다.

평가 결과, 앤트로픽의 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'가 12.0%로 1위를 차지했습니다. 구글의 '제미나이 4 카본'이 10.9%, 오픈AI의 'GPT-6 아스트라'가 9.6%, 메타의 '뮤즈 원더 풀'이 9.0%로 뒤를 이었습니다.

12%란 수치는 실제 업무 100개 중 12개를 완수했다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 과제별 완전 성공 여부와 부분 점수를 반영한 종합 점수입니다. 각 작업에 최대 8시간을 부여하고 세 차례 실행한 성적을 평균했습니다.

중요한 것은 세미애널리시스가 GDPx를 개발한 목적이 AI의 종합적인 지능 측정보다 실제 산업에서 경제적 가치를 창출할 수 있는 능력을 측정하는 데 있다는 것입니다. AI 도입으로 발생하는 초기 매출이 모든 직종에서 고르게 발생하기보다는 자동화 효과가 큰 일부 전문 산업에 집중될 것이라는 판단에서입니다.

이에 따라 전체 직업의 분포나 국내총생산(GDP) 비중 대신 반도체 설계, 금융, 사이버보안, AI 자기 개선 등 고부가가치 분야를 평가 대상으로 선정했습니다. 이번 평가 결과는 2027~2028년 오픈AI와 앤트로픽의 매출을 예측하는 자체 분석에도 활용할 계획입니다.

이 과정에서 기존 실무 평가의 한계도 지적했습니다. 특히 지난해 9월 오픈AI가 공개한 'GDPval'을 사례로 들었습니다. GDPval도 실제 직업에서 수행하는 업무를 평가하지만, 필요한 자료와 지시를 미리 제공한 뒤 보고서나 결과물을 작성하도록 하는 방식에 치중했다는 것입니다. 실제 전문가는 수많은 자료에서 필요한 정보를 직접 찾고, 서로 충돌하는 내용을 비교하며, 명확하게 지시받지 않은 조건까지 판단해야 합니다. 세미애널리시스는 GDPval이 공개 당시에는 획기적인 평가였지만, AI 에이전트가 발전한 현재에는 이러한 능력을 충분히 측정하기 어렵다고 평가했습니다.

기존 벤치마크의 채점 방식에도 문제를 제기했습니다. 일부 평가에서 정답이 잘못 설정됐거나 올바른 해결책을 제출했는데도 오답으로 처리하는 사례가 있다고 지적했습니다. 자체 품질 검증 시스템을 '터미널 벤치 4.0'에 적용한 결과, 전체 과제의 약 50%에서 문제가 발견됐다고 주장했습니다. AI가 문제를 제대로 해결해도 특정 방식으로 답하지 않았다는 이유로 점수를 받지 못할 수 있다는 것입니다.

GDPx는 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해 실제 업무 자료와 프로그램을 포함한 환경을 구축하고, 과제와 채점 기준의 오류까지 검증하도록 설계했습니다. 대표적인 금융 과제에서는 실제 기업 인수 거래를 바탕으로 약 4000개의 익명화된 파일을 포함한 가상 업무 환경을 만들었습니다. AI는 필요한 재무제표와 계약서, 회계자료 등을 직접 찾아 분석하고 기존 문서의 오류를 수정해야 했습니다. 단순히 정리된 자료를 바탕으로 답을 작성하는 것과는 다른 작업입니다.

실제 평가에서 AI 모델들은 복잡한 업무를 끝까지 완수하지 못하는 사례가 많았습니다. 기업의 수익성을 분석하는 한 금융 과제에서는 25차례 실행 가운데 완전히 성공한 사례가 없었습니다. 가장 높은 성적을 거둔 실행도 11개 검증 항목 중 8개만 통과했습니다. 계약 조건과 회계처리 기준을 종합적으로 판단하는 과정에서 실수를 보였습니다. 법률 분야에서도 투자계약 문서를 수정하는 과제에 4개 모델이 총 20차례 도전했지만 모두 완성 기준을 충족하지 못했습니다. 계약상 허점을 놓치거나 기존 합의와 충돌하는 조건을 추가하는 등의 오류가 나타났습니다.

종합 순위와 전문 분야별 성적이 일치하지 않았다는 점도 눈에 띕니다. 오퍼스 5.5는 반도체 설계와 하드웨어 설계, 퀀트 트레이딩에서 가장 높은 점수를 기록했습니다. 제미나이 4 카본은 생물학과 소프트웨어 개발, GPT-6 아스트라는 AI 자기 개선과 재료과학 분야에서 각각 1위를 차지했습니다. 종합 성능이 높은 모델도 모든 전문 분야에서 우수한 것은 아니라는 의미입니다.

그렇다고 기존 AI 벤치마크가 실제 업무를 다루지 않았던 것은 아닙니다. 대표적인 AI 평가업체 아티피셜 애널리시스(AA)도 최근 종합 지능 지수를 개편하면서 'AA 브리프케이스(AA-Briefcase)'와 '프론티어코드 2.0(FrontierCode 2.0)' 등 복잡한 업무 수행 능력을 측정하는 평가를 도입했습니다. GDPx는 이러한 흐름에서 특정 산업의 전문성과 경제적 활용 가능성에 집중했다는 차이가 있습니다. 따라서 GDPx의 낮은 점수를 기존 종합 지수와 직접 비교해 AI 성능이 떨어졌다고 해석할 수는 없습니다.

평가 결과 자체에도 한계는 있습니다. 모델마다 클로드 코드, 코덱스 등 서로 다른 에이전트 실행 환경을 사용했으며, 일부 사이버보안과 생물학 과제에서는 안전장치가 작업을 제한했습니다. 일부 과제의 세부 내용과 채점 기준이 공개되지 않아 외부에서 전체 결과를 독립적으로 재현하기도 어렵습니다.

이번 GDPx는 AI 벤치마크가 실제 업무 수행 능력을 측정하는 데서 나아가 산업별 전문성과 경제적 활용 가치를 검증하는 방향으로 바뀌고 있음을 보여줍니다. 특히 종합 성능이 뛰어난 모델도 모든 전문 분야에서 우수한 것은 아니며, 어려운 문제를 해결하는 능력과 복잡한 업무를 끝까지 완수하는 능력에도 차이가 있었습니다.

AI 에이전트의 산업 현장 도입이 늘면서 이러한 차이를 측정하는 전문 벤치마크도 세분될 것으로 보입니다.

■ 미소스 5.5·GPT-6.2 아스트라 잇달아 포착…최첨단 모델 출시설

앤트로픽 공식 웹사이트에서 '클로드 미소스 5.5'라는 이름이 발견되고, 오픈AI의 'GPT-6.2 아스트라'를 테스트하고 있다는 개발자들의 주장이 나왔습니다. 최근 최첨단 AI 모델에 대한 관심이 높아지면서 출시 전 새로운 모델의 흔적이나 유출 정황도 이전보다 큰 주목을 받는 모습입니다.

■ 구글, '제미나이 4 카본' 공개 사흘 만에 개선판 포착…3D 성능 호평

'제미나이 4 카본'이 공개된 지 사흘 만에 개선 버전인 '카본-H'가 AI 평가 플랫폼에서 테스트 중인 정황이 포착됐습니다. 전작에서 약점으로 지적됐던 3D 모델링과 디자인 성능이 뚜렷한 발전을 이뤘다는 평가가 나왔습니다.

에이전트 50개가 5900개의 메시지를 주고받으며 복잡한 역할 분담과 승인 절차에 매달리다가 마인크래프트 문명 건설에 실패했다는 실험 결과입니다. 여러 AI 에이전트가 실제 업무에서 협업할 때도 불필요한 의사결정과 절차에 빠져 생산성을 떨어뜨릴 수 있다는 점을 보여줬습니다.

Stuck in years-long lines for grid connections and new turbines, some AI data centers are making their own electricity with converted jet engines, the New York Times reported Tuesday.

The engines, pulled from retired aircraft and rebuilt to burn natural gas, aren’t anyone’s idea of a permanent power plant. But they’re another sign of how far power supply has fallen behind the AI buildout.

For companies stuck in those lines, the main draw of converted jet engines is how quickly the engines can be up and running. “It’s all about getting power as fast as possible,” Rystad Energy analyst Audun Martinsen told the Times. With jet-powered units, “they can have a data center running in 24 months,” he said.

Hooking up 100 megawatts to the grid in Northern Virginia, by comparison, takes about seven years , according to the International Energy Agency. Most power capacity is expected to come on by 2031, an executive at Mitsubishi Power, one of the world’s top makers of power generation equipment told Bloomberg last week.

In some cases, these delays are already costing some data center operators business. Last month, Microsoft pulled out as the anchor customer for Nscale’s data center in Loughton, England, after the local utility said it couldn’t deliver enough power until the early-to-mid 2030s.

Elon Musk’s xAI is among the companies already using the engines, having installed eight converted jet-engine turbines in Mississippi to help power its Colossus 2 data center in Memphis, the Times reported, citing state permits and satellite imagery. The units come from ProEnergy, which rebuilds a GE engine commonly found on Boeing jets.

In 2025, OpenAI followed Musk’s lead with gas turbines at its first Stargate site in Abilene, Texas. Crusoe, a Denver-based startup that builds AI data centers, is constructing that Abilene campus and ordered 13 of ProEnergy’s converted units in April.

In September, Crusoe walked away from a $1.25 billion deal to buy 29 natural gas turbines from Boom Supersonic, a startup developing a supersonic passenger jet that has also begun selling a version of that jet’s engine as a power plant for data centers. A Crusoe spokesperson told TechCrunch at the time that the company still plans to use turbines.

Currently the Trump administration is adding to the pressure by encouraging data centers to generate their own electricity.

Converted jet engines come with trade-offs, though: They’re less efficient and pollute more than turbines designed for conventional gas plants and it takes more of them to make the same amount of power, according to the Times. That may ultimately make converted jet engines a short-term play with some experts saying that efficiency and environmental concerns may grow in importance in a year or two.

items.content:
Hackers hijack cPGuard autoupdate to deploy backdoor, steal data

Attackers have compromised the update infrastructure for the cPGuard web security suite to distribute a backdoor and a data-stealing script.

OpsShield, the cPGuard developer, published an alert earlier today saying the attack began on November 2 at 02:06 UTC and affected versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19.

The vendor says that it detected the compromise and stopped the malicious distribution within 12 hours after the attacker pushed the compromised cPGuard versions.

Although the company could not confirm, it said that some servers may have not received and run the malicious script due to update checks occurring at specific intervals.

The attacker leveraged legitimate credentials to gain initial access, although it remains unclear how they were obtained.

“On 2 November 2026 at 02:06 UTC, an unidentified attacker used compromised credentials to gain unauthorized access to OpsShield’s update distribution infrastructure (CDN),” OpsShield said .

“The attacker used this access to distribute a malicious script through the cPGuard update channel.”

cPGuard is a Linux web-server security suite offering malware scanning, firewalls, and attack protection.

It is commonly used by hosting firms and server administrators alongside panels such as cPanel, DirectAdmin, and Plesk. Namecheap offers it on VPS and dedicated servers.

Users updating cPGuard during the compromise window received a script that targeted sensitive data on their machines:

Root database (MariaDB/MySQL) configuration

Root SSH authorization and known-hosts files

The stolen data was uploaded to OpsShield’s licensing server through a compromised account, which the attackers then used to retrieve it.

While OpsShield has not established what data was collected from each server, the company's evidence from the investigation shows that the threat actor retrieved 32 files from each customer.

System administrators are advised to update every cPGuard server to version 5.88.25 or later, reset passwords, and rotate database credentials, cloud secrets, and SSH keys.

OpsShield notes that updating to the latest cPGuard version removes the backdoor and staged files; however, stolen credentials must be invalidated as soon as possible.

The vendor also said that, as an extra precaution, it would release an update to remove previously installed OpsShield support-access keys.

BleepingComputer has contacted OpsShield to learn more about the attack, and a spokesperson told us that the incident has impacted nearly three thousand servers.

"We detected 2946 servers were affected and copied the information mentioned, and our billing system database was copied over as well. We are working on blocking all access, rebuilding the affected systems, and preparing for a public announcement at the earliest possible time," the company representative said.

The company also advises customers to follow the instructions and update cPGuard to version 5.88.25 or later, and reset or rotate credentials that may have been exposed on potentially compromised servers.

OpsShield는 공격자가 CDN을 통해 악성 스크립트를 cPGuard 업데이트 채널로 배포했다고 설명했다. cPGuard는 악성코드 검사 등 기능을 제공하는 Linux 웹서버 보안 제품군이다. 본문이 중간에 끊겨 있어 이후 내용은 확인되지 않는다。

items.summary_ko: 전통 금융사를 대표하는 신생 단체 Capital Markets Alliance가 CFTC의 단일 종목 무기한 선물 승인을 막기 위해 소송을 제기했다. 단체는 Cboe, Citadel Securities 등 주요 거래소와 증권사, 투자사의 지원을 받는다고 밝혔다.
items.content:
A new organization representing traditional financial firms said it filed a lawsuit against the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Tuesday to try to stop the agency's approval of single-stock perpetual futures.

The stock perps are meant to trade in the same way as the regulator's recent roadmap for crypto perps, but Capital Markets Alliance filed the legal challenge on the same day that the agency announced it was giving a green light to open-ended futures contracts for stocks. Though the industry organization doesn't have a significant history, it said it's backed by leading exchanges, broker-dealers and investment firms, including Cboe and Citadel Securities.

Its lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York is seeking to eliminate the policy, arguing that the products are securities-based swaps that belong in the jurisdiction of the Securities and Exchange Commission and contending the CFTC violated the Administrative Procedure Act in failing to offer explanation for its policy and why it contradicts an earlier agency stance.

When CFTC Chairman Mike Selig announced the agency's new policy, he said in a statemen t on Tuesday that it "builds on that milestone by extending the availability of the perpetual futures contract instrument in the U.S. beyond digital commodities and into traditional securities." That move came about five months after the agency had first cleared a path for bitcoin perps, in the hopes that a thriving overseas market would move to the U.S.

The CFTC's earlier action on crypto perps also drew a lawsuit from CME Group. The company similarly argued that the perpetual futures contracts are not actually futures, because they have no end date. They're really swaps, which carry different regulatory treatments, CME contends.

The CFTC didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the new lawsuit.

The lawsuit seems to be the only significant action the CMA has taken so far. A spokesman told CoinDesk the group includes Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets Association among its members.

The regulator's new stance was also criticized by the American Securities Association on Tuesday. "By labeling stock perps as security futures, the CFTC sidestepped the SEC’s jurisdiction and Congress’ ban on selling security-based swaps to retail investors,” said ASA President and CEO Chris Iacovella in a statement.

items.content:
SpaceX joined several other issuers objecting to OKXICE tokenized trading, months after crypto platforms offered tokens tied to its shares.

Just months after tokenized versions of SpaceX shares became one of the biggest drivers of onchain stock trading, the aerospace company is pushing back against plans to bring similar trading to US investors.

According to a Nov. 2 public notice from OKXICE, SpaceX has objected to the proposed listing of tokenized versions of its shares on the trading venue, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). The company now joins Tesla and Amazon among 56 companies objecting to the proposed listings.

Under the Securities and Exchange Commission’s five-year Innovation Exemption introduced in September, platforms such as OKXICE can offer trading in tokenized versions of US stocks without registering as national securities exchanges. But the framework also gives companies a say in the process: They have 30 days to object to the proposed trading of their shares tokenized by third parties, effectively keeping those tokens off the venue.

Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based representations of company shares that allow investors to gain exposure to traditional equities onchain, often around the clock. Depending on the structure, they can be backed by actual shares, although the rights granted to tokenholders may differ from those of traditional shareholders.

OKXICE co-chair and former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo told Cointelegraph on Oct. 20 that the venture expected more objections as companies avoided being the first to test the model.

SpaceX’s objection comes despite tokenized versions of its shares already trading on platforms outside the US, where they have attracted significant trading activity since the company’s June public offering.

Ahead of the SpaceX listing, Backpack Securities, a stock brokerage and tokenization platform, and crypto exchange Kraken, through its xStocks offering, both prepared tokenized versions of the aerospace company’s stock, each designed to be backed by actual shares. Backpack’s SPCX token went on to record $1.08 billion in onchain trading volume in June, while Kraken’s SPCXx token recorded $852 million.

Unlike Backpack and Kraken, OKXICE would open tokenized stock trading to US investors under the SEC’s new regulatory framework, potentially tapping into the world’s largest equity market by capitalization and expanding the investor base for tokenized securities.

Nasdaq warned issuers in September that they “must be cautious about their participation” in the venture, arguing that tokenized stock trading could fragment liquidity and undermine long-term shareholder value.

Despite the growing opposition, Cuomo said during an Oct. 30 press conference that as people see the benefits of tokenization, “you’ll see more and more companies participate.”

Ballistic Ventures, the cybersecurity-focused venture capital firm co-founded by former Kleiner Perkins partner Ted Schlein (pictured above, second from the right), is seeking to raise $490 million across two new funds, TechCrunch has learned through regulatory filings.

The San Francisco-based VC firm filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week to raise $360 million for its third flagship fund, matching the size of its previous fund raised in 2024, and another $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B. Neither fund had recorded any sales at the time of filing.

The fundraising plans come as the growing use of artificial intelligence has raised concerns about more sophisticated cyberattacks. The rise of AI agents has also created new opportunities for cybersecurity startups and the venture capital firms backing them.

Founded in late 2021, Ballistic Ventures’ founding team includes Schlein, former AT&T Cybersecurity president Barmak Meftah and Roger Thornton, who co-founded security companies Fortify Software and AlienVault. The firm has backed companies including Talon Cyber Security, acquired by Palo Alto Networks , and Pangea, bought by CrowdStrike , alongside startups such as Armadin , GetReal, Nudge Security and Oligo Security.

Ballistic’s ties to storied venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins, where Schlein spent more than two decades, help set it apart from rivals, a cybersecurity investor at another VC firm told TechCrunch. Its investment strategy, however, is similar to those of other cybersecurity-focused investors, including Forgepoint Capital and Ten Eleven Ventures, the person said.

In 2022, Ballistic announced its $300 million debut fund and raised another $360 million for its second flagship fund two years later. It also raised about $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund A, per PitchBook data. The new Fund B is targeting a similar amount.

U.S. cybersecurity startups raised $11.5 billion in 2025, the highest since 2022, a recent report by JPMorgan Chase said, citing PitchBook data. AI-enabled companies accounted for about 72% of U.S. cybersecurity venture deals through May this year, compared with 36% in 2019, the report said.

Separately, Microsoft, in its annual Digital Defense Report released last month, warned that hackers are increasingly using AI for activities ranging from phishing and social engineering to malware development. The technology is allowing attackers to operate faster and at greater scale, even as many of their underlying techniques remain unchanged.

Ballistic Ventures declined to comment on its fundraising plans.

items.title: "반도체 쏠림에 가렸다"…3년 연속 이익 늘어도 소외된 종목 [한경우의 케이스스터디]
items.content:
"반도체만 보다가 놓쳤다"…3년째 돈 버는데 몰라본 '이 종목' [한경우의 케이스스터디]

하반기 들어 반도체 호황 지속에 대한 의구심이 커지면서 국내 증시가 흔들리고 있다. 코스피는 지난 7월 말과 10월 중순 두 차례 저점을 만들었고, 외국인은 5월부터 6개월 연속 코스피에서 순매도 행진을 이어갔다. 증권가에서는 그동안 시장의 관심이 반도체주에 쏠렸지만, 이제는 순이익이 꾸준히 증가하는데 주가 측면에서는 소외된 기업을 눈여겨볼 때라는 조언이 나온다.

4일 한국거래소에 따르면 전날 코스피는 3.59% 하락한 5648.79로 거래를 마쳤다. 작년 종가(4214.17)보다는 34.04% 높지만, 지난 6월22일의 종가 기준 고점(9114.55)과 비교하면 38.02% 하락한 상태다.

주가 급락의 배경에는 반도체 호황의 지속성에 대한 의구심이 있다. 미국·이란 전쟁으로 치솟은 국제 유가가 물가를 자극하면서 금리가 상승했고, 이게 인공지능(AI) 투자에 나서는 빅테크 종목의 재원 조달 부담 가중으로 이어진 탓이다. 특히 하나증권은 미국 기술업종의 올해 3분기 자본지출(CAPEX) 증가율이 전년 동기 대비 102%로 정점을 찍은 뒤 내년 4분기 14%까지 낮아질 것으로 예상했다. 인공지능(AI) 인프라 투자 증가세가 둔화하면 국내 반도체 수출과 반도체 기업의 이익 증가세가 꺾일 가능성을 염두에 둬야 한다는 것이다.

코스피 하락도 반도체 대형주가 주도했다. 삼성전자의 전일 종가는 21만9500원으로, 지난 6월18일의 고점(36만2500원) 대비 39.45% 하락했다. SK하이닉스의 고점(6월 22일의 29만1900원) 대비 낙폭은 36.43%다.

이재만 하나증권 연구원은 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스가 기술적 반등을 바탕으로 올해 말부터 내년 1분기까지 지수 반등을 주도하겠지만, 그 이후엔 새로운 주도주가 부상할 가능성에 주목해야 한다고 조언했다.

특히 내년에 주도주로 떠오를 만한 유형 중 하나로 이익은 꾸준히 늘지만 주가는 오랫동안 소외된 기업이 꼽혔다.

한경닷컴은 금융정보업체 에프앤가이드 데이터가이드 서비스를 활용해 △2023년부터 전년 동기 대비 순이익이 3년 연속으로 증가 △올해와 내년에도 순이익 증가가 예상되며 △올해 들어선 뒤 지난 2일까지의 주가 수익률이 코스피(39.0%)보다 20%포인트 이상 낮은 19개 종목을 추렸다. 추려진 종목에는 제약·바이오와 식품·화장품, 금융, 전력기기·방산, 반도체 소재 등 여러 업종이 포함됐다.

삼성바이오로직스는 하나증권이 ‘주식시장에서 소외된 장기 성장주’의 대표 사례로 꼽은 종목이다. 순이익이 2022년 7981억원에서 지난해 1조7844억원으로 3년 새 두 배가 넘는 수준으로 불어났다. 올해와 내년 순이익 컨센서스는 각각 1조8548억원, 2조2050억원이다. 올해 증가율은 3.9%에 그치지만 내년에는 18.9%로 높아질 것으로 전망된다. 그러나 작년 주가 상승률은 21.4% 올라 코스피(76%)에 크게 못 미쳤고, 올해 들어서는 지난 2일까지 15.5% 하락했다.

증권가에서는 실적 성장세가 견조하다는 평가가 나온다. 삼성바이오로직스의 3분기 매출은 1조4903억원, 영업이익은 6401억원으로 시장 기대치를 소폭 웃돌았다. 이달미 상상인증권 연구원은 “1~4공장 완전 가동과 5공장 가동 시작, 미국 락빌 공장 매출 인식이 호실적을 이끌었다”고 분석했다.

삼양식품은 추려진 종목 가운데 이익 규모가 가파르게 늘어난 사례다. 순이익이 2022년 803억원에서 지난해 3887억원으로 3년 만에 4.8배로 불어났다. 올해 5583억원, 내년 6773억원으로 사상 최대 순이익 신기록 행진도 이어갈 것으로 전망된다. 그럼에도 주가는 올해 들어 4.4% 하락했다.

HK이노엔은 올해 주가가 30.1% 하락했다. 코스피 상승률과의 격차는 69.1%포인트, 코스닥 지수와 비교해도 9.5%포인트 낮다. 반면 순이익은 2022년 381억원에서 지난해 757억원으로 매년 늘어 3년 새 약 두 배로 증가했다. 순이익은 올해 853억원, 내년 1001억원으로 증가세가 이어질 것으로 전망된다. 증가율도 올해 12.7%에서 내년 17.4%로 높아질 것으로 예상됐다.

한경우 기자는 한경닷컴에서 주식투자에 대한 기사를 쓰고 있습니다. 개별 종목 분석과 퀀트 투자 콘텐츠에 특히 두각을 나타냅니다.

그는 2014년 농식품 전문 매체에서 기자 생활을 시작했고, 이후 경제매체 산업부로 자리를 옮겨 중화학공업과 해운, 제약·바이오 산업을 출입하며 주요 산업에 대한 이해를 쌓았습니다. 이를 바탕으로 심층적인 종목 분석 기사를 작성하고 있습니다.

‘한경우의 케이스스터디’ 코너에는 주로 퀀트 투자 콘텐츠가 연재되고 있습니다. 에프앤가이드와 코스콤의 데이터 플랫폼을 능숙하게 다루기에 특정 투자지표를 조건 삼아 관심을 가져 볼만한 종목을 선별해 독자들에게 제시합니다.

‘투자톡’ 코너를 통해서는 각 투자 전략을 장기간 시뮬레이션한 백테스트 콘텐츠를 선보이고 있습니다.

items.content:
WorkOS says attacker used ARTEX AI to breach internal sales app

Developer platform WorkOS suffered a data breach after a threat actor accessed business contact records and summaries of customer communications.

According to the company, the attacker used an AI offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts.

Based on evidence from the investigation, no WorkOS app data or production services were accessed or affected.

WorkOS is a developer infrastructure company that provides APIs, SDKs, and tools for integrating services such as enterprise authentication, single sign-on (SSO), user management, and identity management into applications.

According to its website, at least 3,000 companies use its services, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, Perplexity, Snowflake, Plaid, Webglow, and Netlify.

“On October 30, 2026, we identified unauthorized access to an internal WorkOS application used by our sales team,” the company says in an incident alert .

Business contact details (names, email addresses, job titles, and company affiliations from the CRM systems)

Customer account histories (product usage and connection or directory health)

Customer communications (summaries and excerpts from sales calls, support discussions, and customer Slack conversations)

Business account and relationship information (account histories, information about sales and customer relationship)

After detecting the intrusion, WorkOS disabled external access to the affected application and reviewed its access controls on internal tools.

The company also contracted an independent forensics and incident response firm to track the unauthorized activity and determine its full impact.

The company promised to notify affected customers directly, and warned its users to remain vigilant for phishing or social engineering attempts leveraging the exposed information.

WorkOS’s announcement says the attack used an AI-powered offensive security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts.

Company founder Michael Grinich shared more details , saying that the attacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite that has been observed in multiple incidents this year.

Released earlier this year by Chinese developers, the platform was available as an open-source project for offensive security.

ARTEX AI became private after it was used in attacks targeting South Korean banks , but several forks of its code are still available.

More recently, CrowdStrike revealed that cyber-espionage group “Vapor Panda” used the pentesting framework in a global campaign targeting 200 organizations.

Previously, the non-profit cybersecurity organization DIVD also revealed that the same framework powered the attacks it suffered last September .

Grinich explained that the investigating team identified user agents such as ‘artex-enrich/1.0’ and ‘norma/0.4’ in web requests from the threat actor.

The founder assured that the cybersecurity incident has now been fully contained and promised to share more information about the attack after the investigation completes.

Palantir delivered such a huge third-quarter earnings report on Monday that its press release even bragged that the numbers were “crushing consensus expectations.”

Yet, retail investors were lukewarm on the company on Tuesday, with the stock trading slightly down. That’s because Palantir’s enterprise sales, its big growth area, showed signs of slowing.

First, the good news for the company’s investors. Revenue grew 96% year over year to $2.31 billion, the first time it has ever surpassed the $2 billion mark. Palantir’s revenue, which also grew 20% from the previous quarter, beat analysts’ expectations of $2.18 billion. Palantir also reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.44 versus analysts’ expectations of $0.41. The company even upped its revenue guidance for the full year. Normally, that alone would send a stock soaring.

The clincher was that Palantir’s U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever. The company reported $984 million in commercial contracts (up 148% from the year-ago quarter), versus $953 million in U.S. government revenue.

The reason for all this love from enterprises? They are signing up for the company’s AI software that can run frontier models and custom-train open-weight models securely, without sharing any of their data and business processes with outside AI labs. Plus, Palantir has always offered what is today known as “forward-deployed” software engineering, which helps customers customize its wares.

However, Palantir also revealed a less-than-rosy signal: Even as enterprises are moving faster than ever., they are often signing short-term trials.

“What Ryan and I are seeing on the front line and commercial is this much quicker interaction, much quicker to deployment, shorter duration of the contract but then an ability to expand that contract dramatically,” CEO Alex Karp (pictured above) told Wall Street analysts on the quarterly conference call.

Palantir is experiencing one of the unique phenomena of AI in the enterprise right now. Corporations are willing to quickly try AI software without their typical bureaucracy, but they are also more willing to cancel contracts.

Karp used one off-color metaphor after another to describe how unconcerned he was about holding onto his enterprise business.

“We’ve gone from being the most attractive person in the physics department to being the captain of the football team, kind of thing,” he said describing the influx of prospective corporate customers were flowing in. “Conversely, you know, once you go Palantir, you don’t go back, and that’s just that’s how it is, and you see it in our numbers.”

The numbers don’t yet confirm Palantir’s long-term success. While the company closed a hefty $1.46 billion of total contract value from U.S. enterprises in the quarter, that’s actually a decline from its record-setting $2.13 billion of enterprise TCV in the previous quarter. That suggests decelerating sales, at least last quarter.

The next earnings will show if Palantir has solidified its role as a rising U.S. enterprise AI provider. Historically, many enterprises sign their biggest tech purchases in the final quarter of the year. Certainly Karp and team are confident. They increased guidance for U.S. commercial revenue to be “in excess of $3.559 billion, representing a growth rate of at least 143%.”

한국전력공사 등이 출자한 에너지효율화 전문기업 켑코이에스(KEPCO ES)가 더존비즈온 해킹 사고로 주민등록번호와 연락처 등 개인정보가 유출됐을 가능성이 있다고 공식 공지했다. 더존비즈온 해킹 사고 여파가 에너지 분야 기업으로도 확산되고 있다.

켑코이에스는 11월 2일 홈페이지에 개인정보 유출 가능성 안내문을 게시하고, 더존비즈온으로부터 APO 백업서비스 관련 서버에 저장된 일부 암호화 데이터가 외부로 반출된 정황을 통보받았다고 밝혔다.

회사는 개인정보 보호법 제34조 제2항에 따라 유출 가능성을 안내했으며, 현재까지 자사 개인정보의 실제 유출 여부는 확인되지 않았다고 설명했다.

켑코이에스가 공개한 유출 가능 개인정보 항목은 성명, 소속, 직책, 연락처, 주민등록번호, 사업자등록번호 등이다.

다만 해당 정보가 실제로 외부에 유출됐는지는 확정되지 않았다. 개인정보 유출 대상자와 구체적인 항목, 피해 규모는 현재 진행 중인 조사 결과에 따라 달라질 수 있다.

이번 사고는 켑코이에스가 이용하는 더존비즈온의 APO 백업서비스 관련 서버에서 발생했다.

켑코이에스에 따르면 외부 공격자가 더존비즈온의 백업 솔루션 취약점을 악용해 서버에 침입했으며, 서버에 저장된 암호화 데이터 일부가 외부로 반출된 정황이 확인됐다.

더존비즈온은 현재 정확한 사고 발생 시점과 침해 경위를 조사하고 있다. 암호화 키가 외부로 유출된 정황은 발견되지 않았다고 회사 측은 설명했다.

더존비즈온은 사고를 인지한 직후 피해 서버를 강제 종료하고 해외 IP 주소의 접근을 차단하는 등 추가 침해 방지 조치를 시행했다. 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA)에 사고를 신고하고 관계기관 조사에도 협조하고 있다.

켑코이에스는 조사 결과에 따라 실제 개인정보 유출 여부와 대상자, 유출 항목 등이 확인되면 추가 안내할 예정이다.

켑코이에스는 한국전력공사와 발전회사들이 출자해 2016년 설립한 에너지효율화 전문기업이다.

기업과 공공기관 등을 대상으로 에너지 절감 설비 투자, 고효율 기기 보급, 에너지 진단 및 컨설팅, 온실가스 감축 관련 사업을 수행하고 있다.

켑코이에스는 개인정보 유출 가능성이 있는 관계자들에게 금융기관이나 공공기관을 사칭한 전화·문자·이메일에 주의할 것을 당부했다.

특히 금전 이체나 추가 개인정보를 요구하는 연락에 응하지 말고, 출처가 불분명한 인터넷 주소를 클릭하지 않도록 안내했다.

US regulators are opening the door to stock-based perpetual futures, extending a popular crypto trading product into traditional markets amid ongoing legal disputes.

Perpetual futures contracts tied to individual stocks can begin trading on regulated US exchanges for the first time, according to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), extending a derivatives product popularized in cryptocurrency markets into traditional equities.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said in a Tuesday statement that the contracts were deemed approved under CFTC Regulation 40.3 and could be offered on exchanges registered with both the CFTC and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to trade security futures products.

Selig said bringing the products into regulated US markets would allow American traders to access perpetual futures under US regulatory safeguards rather than being “forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues.”

Perpetual futures allow traders to take positions on an asset’s price without owning the underlying asset or facing an expiration date. Crypto exchange BitMEX helped popularize the instruments, commonly referred to as perps, in 2016.

CFTC announces approval of equity perpetual futures trading. Source: CFTC

The announcement follows a wave of regulatory filings in September, when Coinbase, Kalshi and Kraken parent Payward, through its Bitnomial exchange, sought approval to offer perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. OG.com joined the push days later, proposing contracts that could trade around the clock on weekdays.

The filings followed the CFTC’s May approval of Bitcoin perpetual futures contracts for Kalshi and separate regulatory relief allowing Coinbase to provide access to certain cryptocurrency perpetual futures listed on an affiliated foreign exchange.

Selig did not identify which exchanges would offer the contracts or provide a timeline for when trading would begin.

Related: CFTC sues Utah to block action against prediction markets

The announcement also comes nearly three months after President Donald Trump said the CFTC was working to bring Hyperliquid, a decentralized crypto exchange best known for its perpetual futures trading, into the US in a “fully compliant and legal fashion.”

Trump made the remarks during an Aug. 19 White House event . At the time, neither the CFTC nor Hyperliquid had announced a formal plan for bringing the platform to US markets.

However, the CFTC’s approach to perpetual futures has faced legal opposition. In June, CME Group’s Chicago Mercantile Exchange sued the regulator over its approval of cryptocurrency perpetual futures, arguing that the contracts should be regulated as swaps rather than futures and that the agency had exceeded its authority. The distinction matters because swaps are subject to different regulatory requirements, potentially including stricter reporting, margin and registration rules, while futures can trade under the existing futures exchange framework.

The CFTC moved to dismiss the lawsuit in September, arguing that CME lacked standing because it had not demonstrated financial harm and could list similar contracts itself.

Meanwhile, the Capital Markets Alliance, a coalition that includes Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets, filed a lawsuit Tuesday afternoon seeking to overturn the CFTC’s approval.

The group argues that the contracts are security-based swaps under the SEC’s jurisdiction and that the CFTC violated the Administrative Procedure Act by failing to adequately explain its decision or consider the potential impact on investors. The lawsuit also seeks to prevent the approvals from taking effect while the case proceeds.

items.content:
Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says North Korean hackers used a fake job interview to trick an employee into installing malware that ultimately let them compromise the company's wallet infrastructure and steal about $6.34 billion in digital assets.

This new information was shared in an incident report published today, which details how the attackers used social engineering, malicious software, and compromised internal systems to carry out the October 29 crypto theft.

As previously reported by BleepingComputer, the FBI attributed the attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor, also tracked as Lazarus Group, Jade Sleet, and APT38.

Binance says the attack began in September when a software engineer was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform by someone impersonating a Project Director at a fictitious company.

The employee's profile referenced his experience at Binance, making him a valuable target for attackers looking to breach the cryptocurrency exchange.

The fake recruiter scheduled two interviews for the employee, first with someone posing as a human resources representative, then with another individual claiming to be the company's CEO.

During the first interview, the fake HR representative held a live video call and shared a social media account with personal photos and videos to build trust.

The second interview took place through a popular social chat application where the employee was instructed to download a coding assignment from an online code repository.

According to Binance, the repository contained malicious code that, when executed, compromised the employee's device with previously unseen custom malware that antivirus software did not detect.

"The malware employed sophisticated obfuscation and evasion techniques, including replacing a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version to execute commands and establish communication with an attacker-controlled external server," explained Binance.

"The 0-day malware was not detected by the endpoint security protection tools at the time. The attacker also took steps to conceal the malicious activity and remove traces of the compromise, making detection and subsequent investigation more challenging."

Binance explained that the malicious script created a replacement executable named pyenv_ in the macOS Homebrew installation directory.

The script then deleted the legitimate pyenv executable, renamed the malicious file to pyenv , modified its symbolic link, and used it to spawn a Z shell ( zsh ) process.

The malicious replacement allowed the attackers to execute commands received from an attacker-controlled server.

By October 20, the attackers had used the compromised engineer's computer and an internal AI tool to compromise two additional employees working on Binance's wallet infrastructure, obtaining credentials and a container deployment token.

On October 29, the hackers used the stolen credentials to deploy a malicious script and gain unauthorized access to Binance's wallet signing service, allowing them to transfer billions of dollars in cryptocurrency across multiple blockchains.

The attackers also abused Ethereum's EIP-7702 authorization mechanism, allowing them to continue stealing cryptocurrency even after the exchange suspended withdrawals.

Binance says it has since rebuilt affected systems, replaced compromised devices, and revoked stolen credentials.

As of November 3, approximately $2.85 billion in stolen assets had been frozen or intercepted, while 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of October 31.

Binance says it is continuing to investigate the breach and has brought in independent security firms to review its findings.

items.content:
Image: Glenn Carstens Peters via Unsplash Google dismantles massive botnet hidden in Android TV boxes

Google along with several cybersecurity companies and Japanese law enforcement dismantled a global botnet called X.CPE that was hidden in more than 1.3 million set-top boxes across more than 200 countries.

Google said it tied the scheme to Videostrong Technology, a Chinese company that was an Android original equipment manufacturer producing a range of screens, speakers and robots.

The overwhelming majority of the infected devices in the X.CPE botnet are Android TV set-top boxes, Google said, adding that they observed a number of other infected Android-based IoT devices, including telehealth devices, karaoke machines and digital signage devices.

In lengthy reports about the scheme, Google and other cyber investigators accused Videostrong of monetizing the backdoor by “selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices.”

“We found this malicious software built directly into many different device models and brands over multiple years, supported by dedicated infrastructure and constantly evolving configurations to evade detection and manage their affiliates,” Google said.

“We believe this campaign wasn’t an isolated rogue insider or a development oversight. As a result, Google has cut ties with Videostrong and banned them from making devices with preloaded Google apps.”

Videostrong did not respond to requests for comment. The company says it has worked as an original equipment manufacturer for more than 14 years and sells a variety of AI-backed devices.

Google said Videostrong was allegedly turning infected devices into a residential proxy network and loading other types of malware onto X.CPE-compromised devices.

The botnet generated revenue from the devices by reselling bandwidth, data exfiltration, delivering video content, ad fraud, loading additional backdoors and installing apps for payment. The software allowed third-party traffic to pass through a person’s internet connection, using their internet address and bandwidth.

X.CPE was embedded in the device’s firmware before it even reached a person’s home and was built to evade security checks. Videostrong allegedly continued to change the malware used, updating it in 2024 and 2026.

Google worked with Japanese police, as well as cybersecurity firms TrendAI, Human and Synthient, to disrupt the domains that underpinned the botnet.

“Our research identified over 1.3 million devices affected by this campaign,” said Robert McArdle, director of cybercrime research at TrendAI. “That's millions of households and businesses completely unaware that their equipment was being used as an accessory in active criminality — whether defrauding advertisers or piggybacking on their connections to carry out other attacks via residential proxies — which would commonly include identity theft impersonating people in their region.”

According to Google, Videostrong used “obfuscation techniques” to pass its security tests and load the malware onto the devices. Google pledged to change its review process to stop future manufacturers from conducting similar campaigns.

Google said it took legal action to take down the domains Videostrong used to control the botnet and install the malware while also suing to destroy the domains used by other malware families loaded onto the devices.

But they noted that even if a user tried to uninstall the malware, it would automatically reinstall, according to cybersecurity researchers. The backdoor was able to silently download other files onto the device and execute them without user consent.

Google did not explain if customers with infected devices will be notified or if there is any effort to forcibly remove malware from compromised devices as U.S. law enforcement agencies have done in other similar botnet cases .

items.content:
Rapid LLM development is outrunning the research meant to explain it, study finds

View the LinkedIn Profile of Matthias Bastian

Stanford researchers Owen Queen and James Zou tested 50 widely cited claims about large language models against 20 models and found that 44 percent have already "expired." Among the 22 findings with an estimated expiration date, the average lifespan was just 15.7 months.

The two examined the claims using models released between July 2024 and September 2026 by eight different developers. The original effect behind the expired findings has largely disappeared, while another 34 percent have weakened significantly. Only 16 percent still hold, and 6 percent have actually gotten stronger. After one year, 16 percent had expired. After two years, that number climbed to 39 percent.

Claims about what models can't do expire fastest, according to the study . Five of nine reasoning-related findings are considered expired, and none have held up or gotten stronger. They include well-known weaknesses like counting letters in "strawberry," arithmetic in unfamiliar number systems , losing information in the middle of long contexts , and giving up correct answers when users push back. The researchers suspect these kinds of errors have a "correct" outcome, giving developers a clear target to train toward.

The Stanford study found that 44 percent of reviewed LLM findings have expired, with another 34 percent weakened. All nine reasoning findings have faded, while sycophancy, deception and strategic behavior has the most findings that persist or have strengthened. | Image: Queen and Zou

Claims about preferences and tendencies prove longer-lived. Of the 11 findings that have held or gotten stronger, three involve LLM behavior as evaluators. They prefer their own answers , rate accepted and rejected papers similarly, and are swayed by linguistic spin in medical abstracts. Three more involve sycophancy and agreement toward users . Moreover, there's a left-leaning political bias , near-identical answers to open-ended questions, and a non-uniform distribution when generating random numbers.

Hallucinated references dropped from 55 percent to zero, but not everywhere

As a case study, Queen and Zou looked at the fabrication of scientific citations . In the original 2023 study by Walters and Wilder, GPT-3.5 made up 55 percent of its references. The Stanford researchers sent the same prompts to current models. GPT-6.1 Sol fabricated 0 percent, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 came in at 1 percent. But Qwen3.7-Flash, also a 2026 model, still fabricated 69 percent of its references in the same test.

The study warns against reading these results as an all-clear. On so-called two-hop questions, where a model has to combine two known facts, Claude Sonnet 5.5 still fails in about 10 percent of cases where it correctly answers both individual questions. The original paper reported 43 percent for ChatGPT. The "Reversal Curse" and contradictory answers to paired time-related questions have weakened too, but they're still detectable.

Social biases are a mixed case, according to the researchers. The left-leaning political bias persists, while gender stereotypes and implicit association biases have weakened. Biases against speakers of African American English have actually flipped direction in the trend data.

Model-to-model gaps remain wide even within the same generation

Results vary considerably across models, even within the same release window. Among models released between July and September 2026, the number of expired findings ranges from 11 for DeepSeek V4 Pro to 30 for GPT-6.1 Sol. Neither release date, provider, nor model size reliably predicts the pattern.

Queen and Zou draw a broad conclusion. Empirical findings about LLMs should be presented as observations about specific models at a specific point, not as general truths. Papers should document the model, version, and date, and publish prompts and analysis code so findings can be…

Kalshi and Polymarket price a 75% chance of a Democratic sweep, days after markets misjudged Brazil’s runoff.

Update (Nov. 3 at 10:32 p.m. UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from Talos.

As Americans across the country head to the polls for the US midterm elections Tuesday, prediction market traders have spent months wagering on the outcome. According to an analysis by The Washington Post, nearly $1.9 billion in election-related contracts had traded on Kalshi and Polymarket as of Monday, marking record trading activity for a midterm election cycle.

Markets on both platforms favor Democrats winning control of Congress, with a Democratic sweep priced at 75% on Kalshi and 75.5% on Polymarket as of 4:30 pm UTC. Kalshi traders gave Democrats a 93% chance of taking the House and a 75% chance of winning the Senate, while Polymarket priced those outcomes at 94.5% and 75.5% , respectively.

The vote comes nine days after prediction markets failed to anticipate the outcome of Brazil’s presidential election, with Flávio Bolsonaro favored at roughly 80% the day before incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the runoff. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour reportedly cautioned that “a 5% probability doesn’t mean it won’t happen,” according to CNBC.

For the crypto industry, a shift in congressional control could reshape the prospects for long-awaited regulatory clarity.

A key race for crypto has centered on the Senate seat in Ohio, where Defend American Jobs, part of the Fairshake super PAC network, allocated 54% of its total expenses. According to the official website, $36.9 million was spent on supporting Senator Jon Husted and $19.7 million opposing the staunch crypto critic, Democrat Sherrod Brown. Fairshake spent $40 million to help unseat Brown in 2024.

However, the flood of spending may be to no avail, with traders expecting a win for Brown. The Kalshi market for the race predicted a 72% chance for a Brown win and 72.5% on Polymarket, both in line with a final New York Times/Siena poll that had him ahead 49% to 44%.

A Brown victory could complicate the crypto industry’s legislative agenda, particularly if Democrats regain control of the Senate. Analysts have identified him as a potential chairman of the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, although the leadership position remains uncertain.

Related: From Uptober to Hacktober: Are Bitcoin’s seasonal patterns becoming obsolete?

In Maine, however, a Democratic win predicted by traders could help the crypto industry expand its influence in Washington. Republican Senator Susan Collins was one of four Republicans who voted against advancing the CLARITY Act in September, stalling the bill in the Senate.

Kalshi gives Democrat Troy Jackson a 71% chance of unseating her, while Polymarket puts his chances at 71.5% , broadly in line with New York Times polls conducted in October that had Jackson ahead by two percentage points. Advocacy group Stand with Crypto rates Jackson as strongly supportive of crypto, potentially giving the industry another ally in the Senate should he win.

Although many prediction markets are broadly in line with polling results, traders have made clearer calls in three states where polls show close races.

In Alaska, Kalshi gives Democrat Mary Peltola a 71% chance of defeating Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, even though the final New York Times/Siena poll had her ahead by just two percentage points, 48% to 46%. Both candidates have expressed strong support for crypto, according to Stand With Crypto.

In South Carolina, where the candidates were tied at 48% in the New York Times/Siena poll, Kalshi gives Republican Senator Darline Graham, a crypto supporter, a 71% chance of defeating Democrat Annie Andrews.

Iowa remains a toss-up on both platforms, with Democrat Josh Turek overtaking Republican Representative Ashley Hinson on Polymarket at 52% , after months of Hinson being favored to win.

Fal , a San Francisco-based startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, has raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported .

The startup announced its Series E and F rounds at the same time, noting that a combined $1.65 billion was raised across both. (Sequoia led the earlier round.)

The latest round (Series F) comes amid soaring demand for inference services, the process of running an AI model that’s already been trained to generate outputs, particularly from customers relying on open source models. Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, Bloomberg’s report noted.

Companies providing inference services, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Modal, have also been growing rapidly and raising large funding rounds at higher valuations . But their gross margins remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing compute, according to several people familiar with inference companies’ financials.

Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader and Oracle engineer, and Gorkem Yurtseven, who was previously a developer at Amazon.

items.title: Google: LLMjacking attacks rack up $1 million in cloud AI charges
items.summary: Large language model hijacking attacks, also known as LLMjacking, are generating large fraudulent cloud charges, with some organizations losing more than $100,000 per day. [...]
items.content:
Google: LLMjacking attacks rack up $1 million in cloud AI charges

Large language model hijacking attacks, also known as LLMjacking, are generating large fraudulent cloud charges, with some organizations losing more than $100,000 per day.

Companies can record costs as high as $1 million due to fraudulent calls using stolen API keys, researchers at Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant in analyzed incidents.

Based on their observations, there are "two distinct operational clusters coordinating to compromise and monetize enterprise LLM infrastructure."

The researchers identified two categories of threat actors: those who scan for publicly exposed LLM endpoints and those who steal valid API keys from unprotected machines.

After gaining initial access, the attackers sell it to services known as LLM mixers, which provide their subscribers with unauthorized access to LLMs.

Once access is resold, request volumes can spike suddenly, sometimes exceeding 1,000 requests per second. The service provider records the requests as legitimate consumption and charges the victim organization for the tokens.

GTIG and Mandiant observed an increase in this type of activity this year, with fraudulent charges exceeding $100,000 in a single day, and cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1,000,000.

LLM mixers offer access to AI resources at very low prices, using their proxy infrastructure to relay customers' prompts to hijacked services through stolen API keys.

The researchers found several examples of such relaying infrastructure, including Jet Night, which sells “unlimited access plans” for $60/month, and the newapi[.]pro service.

“Another threat actor that executed more than 500,000 LLM API calls in less than eight hours leveraged stolen third-party API keys to power the token routing service jet-night.com,” Google says .

“Jet Night passed nearly one million dollars in token costs to the victim organization.”

Google also identified the threat cluster UNC6993, which appears to use gateway tools to aggregate stolen keys and distribute requests, and likely sells access via underground forums.

The attackers gain access via exposed or compromised cloud credentials, service account keys, GitHub tokens, active session tokens, and LLM API keys.

Attackers search the compromised environment for credentials, logs, databases, and secret managers, and try to create backdoor accounts or inject SSH keys to maintain persistent access.

The researchers have also observed threat actors exploiting CVE-2026-40217, a vulnerability in LiteLLM that allows running arbitrary code on the server by leveraging the custom-code guardrail testing endpoint.

In some cases, Google says that attackers used the victim's cloud infrastructure to host unauthorized proxy endpoints and agentic workloads.

"For example, one threat actor enabled agents, deployed publicly accessible reverse proxies, and used custom Node.js proxy bundles to expose endpoints compatible with multiple frontier LLMs rebranded under a persona known as D1337-KAIROS," the researchers say.

Google recommends several actions to protect against LLMjacking attacks, which start with prioritizing Identity and Access Management (IAM) and securing the supply chain.

Companies should use centralized secrets platforms to enable the rotation and management of sensitive keys and secrets. Users should not have extended privileges unless required by their role and tasks.

"Deny all permissions that are not explicitly required, including access to Cloud LLM services," Google recommends.

Enforcing phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA), ensuring monitoring tools provide comprehensive visibility across the environment to identify unauthorized LLM and AI services (shadow AI), and setting API usage and spending limits can help organizations detect LLMjacking attacks early, limit their impact, or prevent them altogether.

items.title: mSecure Warns Users to Change Passwords, Reset 2FA and Passkeys After Suspicious Activity
items.summary: Customers of the mSecure password manager are being urged to act now to protect the confidential information they store in it, possibly by changing passwords, resetting two-factor authentication (2FA), and removing passkeys. The warning came in an email sent on November 3 in the
items.content:
Customers of the mSecure password manager are being urged to act now to protect the confidential information they store in it, possibly by changing passwords, resetting two-factor authentication (2FA), and removing passkeys.

The warning came in an email sent on November 3 in the name of developer mSeven Software. It says the company recently learned of suspicious activity linked to the app but does not say what happened or whether anyone's stored data was exposed.

The email says it went to current and former mSecure customers. A customer who received it posted its text in a thread on mSecure's support forum on November 3.

As of 18:00 UTC on November 3, mSeven had posted nothing about the email on mSecure's X and Facebook accounts. No staff member had replied in that forum thread.

The email says mSeven started an investigation, took steps to limit the problem and brought in outside cybersecurity experts. It does not name the systems involved, say when the activity happened or whether it has stopped, or give the number of people who received the email.

mSecure can sync a customer's vault through mSecure Cloud, Dropbox, iCloud or Wi-Fi. The email does not say whether it matters which of these a customer uses.

mSecure 7 can keep passkeys and 2FA codes in the vault next to passwords, on its Essentials plan and above. The email's advice is about protecting information stored in mSecure. The email does not say whether the 2FA and passkey steps cover those stored items, the mSecure account's own sign-in, or both.

mSecure says vault data is encrypted on the customer's device before it is synced, and that even its developers cannot access customers' information.

In mSecure 6.1.5 for Android, mSeven could, in theory, access stored data, according to Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), which found this in a study published in December 2025 . The BSI tested only that version, and its results may have changed with later updates.

The email does not say whether the suspicious activity reached vault data or the keys that protect it.

The email offers its steps as possibilities and does not say which accounts to deal with first or how to carry out each step. It also does not say whether customers should keep using mSecure, including to store their new passwords.

As of 18:00 UTC on November 3, the newest iPhone version of mSecure in Apple's App Store was 7.1.0, released on October 23.

items.title: Several German lawmakers and foreign policy staff received Apple warnings on spyware
items.summary: Members of Germany's political elite were among the spyware targets in 99 countries that Apple personally warned recently.
items.content:
View of the German parliament (Bundestag) from the dome above. Image: Christian Lue via Unsplash Several German lawmakers and foreign policy staff received Apple warnings on spyware

Multiple lawmakers and public figures in Germany are among the snooping victims Apple warned last week about spyware attacks, according to the country’s information security agency.

The hacking attempts are a significant development underscoring the national security threat European officials face as spyware deployment becomes both increasingly visible and apparently inexorable under current policies on the continent.

They also spotlight Europe’s continuing vulnerability to snooping, which human rights and digital freedoms advocates have loudly demanded lawmakers address more aggressively.

On Monday, the German news magazine Der Spiegel reported the Apple threat notifications were sent to members of a German delegation of federal ministries’ staffers, lawmakers and journalists traveling with Chancellor Friedrich Merz on a sweep through Asia. While there Merz met with top officials in South Korea, Japan and Singapore.

Many of the victims have not come forward, but on Tuesday morning, Franziska Brantner, co-leader of the Green Party and a member of the parliament’s European Affairs Committee, revealed she was among the victims, whom Apple said were located in 99 countries.

The information security agency, known as the BSI, on Friday sent German officials, lawmakers and public figures who received the threat notifications a warning letter saying they should assume their devices are infected and immediately replace them, according to a local news outlet’s interview with Digital Minister Karsten Wildberg.

The letter was sent within 24 hours of Apple sending the threat notifications, which Wildberg said highlights that the government “reacted super quickly.”

The BSI said it does not know how many of the victims’ devices were actually infected versus merely targeted or why those receiving the alerts were pinpointed by hackers, but its announcement and letter alone make clear that it considers the attacks to be particularly noteworthy.

Late last week, a Lebanese documentary filmmaker and Turkey-based reporter were the first victims to publicly confirm they were among scores, if not hundreds, of targets that received Apple warnings about spyware targeting.

Hannah Neumann, a member of the European Parliament representing Germany, has long advocated for European lawmakers and officials to step up their efforts to combat spyware. She served on parliament’s PEGA committee — now disbanded — to investigate advanced commercial spyware, particularly the NSO Group’s frequently abused Pegasus software.

In July, Neumann spoke out after spyware was discovered on the phone of a former parliamentarian who also sat on the investigating committee. The latest revelations further emphasize security threats advanced commercial spyware poses, she said.

“Several foreign policy politicians and also staffers have received Apple notifications in the last round, and given that before it was maybe one in one round and then maybe another one in another round, this has been very different this time,” Neumann said in an interview. “There has been something big going on.”

Neumann has long called spyware abuses a national security threat in addition to an invasion of privacy.

Netflix announced on Tuesday that it’s rolling out a new “AI Discover” tab where users will be able to experiment with new ways to find their next watch. The first experimental feature launching under the tab will allow users to get recommendations based on what they’re currently in the mood for.

Users can choose from curated themes featuring clips from shows and movies, based on their mood, viewing preferences, how much time they have, or what’s new and trending. Themes include “something light,” “scare me,” “family movie night,” “quick watches,” and more.

The addition of the new tab suggests that Netflix wants to make its growing library easier to navigate while shifting discovery away from an experience where users are endlessly scrolling through titles toward a more personalized and AI-powered experience.

Netflix says AI Discover is powered by a new intelligence layer it’s been building that responds to what users tell the platform in real time and keeps learning.

Once users pick a theme, they’ll see matching recommendations. They also have the option to select more specific themes so they can keep searching until they find something they’re interested in, or choose the “something different” option to start over. Each title features a “Tune Your Recommendations” button beside “Play” and “My List” to allow users to save recommendations they like or exclude titles they don’t want suggested again.

“There’s more to enjoy and discover on Netflix than ever, but what sounds right for a quiet night in may look different for family movie night or a few spare minutes,” Netflix wrote in a blog post . “We’ve spent years refining how you discover, with recommendations tailored to your tastes, from what you Thumbs Up to what you add to ‘My List.’ Now, AI Discover joins the mix as a new way to explore.”

Netflix describes AI Discover as its “test kitchen,” where it will “try out new recipes for discovery.” The company says users’ feedback will help it decide which features to keep or improve before bringing them over to the main Netflix experience.

AI Discover is starting to roll out in the U.S. to users who use Netflix in English on supported TVs. The company plans to bring the new tab to additional users in the coming weeks.

If users have access to the new feature, they’ll see a “Discover” button with a red gem icon and a “New” label in the top navigation bar on their TV.

items.summary: Blockchain infrastructure provider Chainstack on Tuesday disclosed that it was targeted in a cyber attack that allowed an unauthorized party to gain access to some parts of its infrastructure. The incident is assessed to be part of a large-scale, artificial intelligence (AI)-powe
items.content:
Blockchain infrastructure provider Chainstack on Tuesday disclosed that it was targeted in a cyber attack that allowed an unauthorized party to gain access to some parts of its infrastructure.

The incident is assessed to be part of a large-scale, artificial intelligence (AI)-powered attack campaign that came to light last week.

"An external attacker gained unauthorized access to part of Chainstack's infrastructure through a third-party component," the company said . "We detected the intrusion, cut the access paths, and are hardening our systems."

According to the timeline of events shared by Chainstack, the attacker gained access to a development environment on October 26, 2026, and then escalated their access to break into "some parts of our production environment."

The intrusion was subsequently detected on October 31, 2026, and the attacker's access was cut off that same day, the company noted.

As part of the digital break-in, the threat actor is said to have accessed a database containing customer account information, including organization names, account holder names, the email addresses of organization’s members on Chainstack, and password hashes.

"The attacker also had access to systems holding node credentials," Chainstack said. "We have no evidence they were read, but we are treating them as exposed and ask customers to rotate them."

Besides rotating the node credentials, customers are advised to regenerate their platform API keys, update passwords -- including other services where the same password has been reused -- and remain alert to potential phishing attempts.

Although Chainstack did not disclose any specifics about the attack, it's assessed to share overlaps with a campaign undertaken by a China-linked cluster to target high-value firms using ARTEX.

The development comes as API platform WorkOS also disclosed a security incident that involved the same autonomous AI agent framework to conduct offensive security operations. The incident, which was discovered on October 30, 2026, was limited to its GTM systems, and did not affect production systems or customer platform data.

The breach is part of a growing trend in which AI agents are being employed to devise tailored attack strategies and automate different phases of the intrusion.

"This increases the speed and scale of attacks that exploit weaknesses such as exposed applications and stolen credentials," WorkOS said. "It increases the need for timely remediation and monitoring that can connect suspicious activity across systems."

Last week, blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis also revealed that it detected an "external actor using offensive agentic techniques" to obtain access to its systems and internal tools. As of November 2, 2026, the company has proactively taken its Reactor and Data Solutions products offline.

"We are closely monitoring these systems for unusual activity and will keep you apprised of new information so you can make informed decisions for your business and operations," Chainalysis said .

Another organization to be hit by ARTEX is the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD). The September 21, 2026, breach involved the exploitation of two zero-day flaws in the open-source Zammad ticketing system (CVE-2026-102489 and CVE-2026-102490), enabling attackers to escalate privileges, run code remotely, and exfiltrate data.

items.content:
일론 머스크 CEO가 AI 에이전트 '그록 봇(Grok Bot)'의 운영 비용이 매출에 비해 지나치게 높다며 이용자 사용량 제한을 정당화했다. 최근 일부 이용자의 주간 사용 한도가 예상보다 빠르게 소진되는 현상이 나타난 가운데, 서비스 운영 비용을 줄이기 위한 조치로 풀이된다.

머스크 CEO는 1일(현지시간) X를 통해 "그록 봇을 제공하는 비용이 매출에 비해 지속할 수 없을 정도로 높았다"고 밝혔다.

지난 주말부터 이용자들이 사용량 한도가 평소보다 빠르게 줄어든다고 불만을 제기하자, 직접 원인을 설명한 것이다.

일부 이용자는 서비스를 사용하지 않았는데도 주간 사용량이 50%에서 100%로 급증했다고 주장했다. 평소에는 한도에 도달하지 않았지만, 이번에는 사용량 초기화까지 나흘이나 남은 상황에서 한도를 모두 소진했다는 사례도 나왔다.

머스크는 한 이용자가 사용량 제한에 불만을 제기하자 "더 높은 사용량 요금제로 전환하는 비용이 부담스럽냐"는 취지로 반문했다. 이어 다른 게시물에서는 사용량 한도를 줄이고 이를 이용자에게 알리는 것은 "그저 합리적인 조치"라고 밝혔다.

다만 실제 한도를 얼마나 축소했는지, 앞으로 어떤 기준으로 제한을 적용할지는 구체적으로 공개하지 않았다.

The cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 1, 2026

그록 봇은 가상 컴퓨터를 활용해 쇼핑 등 다양한 작업을 이용자 대신 수행하는 AI 에이전트다. 스페이스X가 지난 8월 출시했으며, 무료부터 월 200달러 요금제까지 여러 구독 상품으로 제공한다.

요금제별로 주간 사용량 한도를 두고 매주 초기화하는 방식이다. 대규모 AI 연산으로 발생하는 비용을 통제하기 위한 조치로, 메타의 AI 에이전트 등 다른 서비스에서도 유사한 방식을 채택하고 있다.

이용자는 빠르게 늘고 있다. 스페이스X가 지난달 공개한 실적 자료에 따르면 그록 봇의 주간 유료 이용자는 80만명에 달했다. 당시 머스크는 "내가 경험한 제품 가운데 가장 빠르게 성장하는 서비스"라고 평가했다. 이어 그록 봇이 스페이스X의 '초지능(Super Intelligence)' 부문 컴퓨팅 자원을 가장 많이 사용하는 서비스가 될 수 있다고 전망했다.

최근 그록 봇을 월 8달러짜리 'X 구독' 상품에 포함하겠다는 계획도 발표했다. 해당 상품에는 X 프리미엄과 스페이스X가 인수한 AI 코딩 플랫폼 커서(Cursor)도 포함된다. 머스크는 지난 10월 그록 봇이 그록 외에도 클로드 오퍼스 5.5, 미드저니, 수노 등 다른 AI 모델을 활용할 것이라고 밝힌 바 있다.

AI 에이전트가 기술 업계의 새로운 성장 동력으로 주목받고 있지만, 수익성 확보는 여전히 과제로 남아 있다. 메타의 AI 에이전트 '뮤즈(Muse)'도 이용자가 1000만명을 넘어섰지만, 마크 저커버그 CEO는 지난달 실적 발표에서 "컴퓨팅 자원을 매우 많이 소비하는 서비스"라며 아직 수익을 내지 못하고 있다고 설명했다.

그록 봇의 운영 비용을 둘러싼 머스크의 발언은 AI 서비스의 성장과 수익성 사이에 놓인 간극을 보여준다. 이용자가 늘어날수록 추론과 작업 수행에 필요한 컴퓨팅 비용도 커지는 만큼, 무제한 사용을 제공하기보다 요금제별 한도를 조정하는 방식이 당분간 이어질 가능성이 있다.

items.content:
뤼튼테크놀로지스의 '크랙'과 스캐터랩의 '제타'가 주도해 온 AI 캐릭터챗 시장에 게임사들이 진출하고 있다. 크래프톤이 K팝 팬덤을 겨냥한 서비스를 출시한 데 이어 컴투스도 관련 플랫폼 개발에 착수하면서 경쟁이 본격화할 조짐이다.

크래프톤과 컴투스가 대표적이다. 크래프톤은 지난 2일 K팝에 특화된 AI 캐릭터챗 '키프(Kiff)'를 출시했다. 첫 협업 대상은 걸그룹 피프티피프티로 이용자는 멤버들이 직접 페르소나와 외형을 구상한 캐릭터와 대화하며 팬덤 활동을 즐길 수 있다. 월 3900원에 무제한 채팅이 가능하다.

게임사들은 캐릭터와 세계관을 설계하고 이용자의 참여를 유지하는 데 축적한 경험을 AI 캐릭터챗에 활용할 수 있다. 크래프톤은 게임 속 캐릭터와 이용자의 자연스러운 상호작용을 연구해 온 기술을 K팝 팬덤 서비스에 적용했다고 설명했다.

컴투스도 여성향 AI 캐릭터 채팅 플랫폼 개발에 착수했다. 최근 콘텐츠·시스템 기획자 채용에 나섰으며, 대형언어모델(LLM) 기반 캐릭터 상호작용과 호감도 시스템, 대화 시나리오 등을 개발할 계획이다.

크래프톤의 K팝 AI 캐릭터챗 서비스 '키프(Kiff)' (사진=크래프톤)

다른 게임사들은 아직 독립적인 캐릭터챗 서비스 출시에 신중하다. 넷마블은 AI 기술을 게임 개발 업무의 효율성을 높이는 데 활용하고 있으며, 별도 캐릭터챗 서비스는 준비하지 않고 있다고 밝혔다. 넥슨도 관련 계획이 없다고 설명했다.

카카오게임즈는 자체 게임에 AI 챗봇을 접목하는 방식을 택했다. MMORPG '도깨비의 세계'에 이용자의 플레이 상황을 분석해 성장 방향을 안내하는 AI 챗봇 '묘롱'을 도입했다.

기존 캐릭터챗 업체들도 게임업계와 접점을 넓히고 있다. 뤼튼은 오는 19~22일 부산 벡스코에서 열리는 '지스타 2026' 메인 스폰서를 맡았다. 게임사가 아닌 AI 기업이 지스타 메인 스폰서를 맡은 것은 이번이 처음이다. 지스타 조직위원회는 AI와 스토리텔링을 결합한 서비스라는 점을 선정 이유로 꼽았다.

다음 달 일산 킨텍스에서 열리는 애니메이션 게임 축제 'AGF 2026'에도 푸딩 AI와 베이비챗, 위프 등 캐릭터챗 서비스가 대거 참가한다.

관건은 수익 구조와 안전성이다. 캐릭터챗은 대화량이 늘수록 추론 비용이 커지지만, 수익은 정액 구독이나 광고에 의존한다.

글로벌 AI 캐릭터챗 업체 캐릭터닷AI는 월간 활성 이용자(MAU) 1200만명을 확보하고도 컴퓨팅 비용과 인건비, 매출 부진, 법적 분쟁 등이 겹치면서 매월 800만~900만달러의 손실을 기록했다. 결국 지난달 미국에서 파산보호를 신청했다.

캐릭터닷AI는 청소년의 자해와 자살에 영향을 미쳤다는 소송에도 직면했다. AI 캐릭터챗 업체들이 이용자를 확보하는 것뿐 아니라 대화 비용을 감당할 수 있는 수익 구조와 청소년 보호 장치까지 갖춰야 한다는 점을 보여준다.

items.title: 카르파시, 유튜브 추천에 질려 AI로 대안 개발…"2시간 만에 완성"
items.summary: 안드레이 카르파시 오픈AI 공동 창립자가 유튜브의 자극적인 썸네일과 반복적인 추천 콘텐츠에 불만을 느껴 AI를 활용한 대안 서비스 '해커튜브(HackerTube)'를 개발했다. 해커뉴스(Hacker News)의 댓글 4300만개를 분석해 영상 6454개를 선정하고, 앤트로픽의 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'를 활용해 약 2시간 만에 서비스를 구축했다고 밝혔다.현재 앤트로픽에 재직 중인 카르파시는 31일(현지시간) 자신의 블로그를 통해 해커튜브를 소개하고, 이어 X를 통해 개발 과정과 주요 기능을 공개했다
items.content:
안드레이 카르파시 오픈AI 공동 창립자가 유튜브의 자극적인 썸네일과 반복적인 추천 콘텐츠에 불만을 느껴 AI를 활용한 대안 서비스 '해커튜브(HackerTube)'를 개발했다. 해커뉴스(Hacker News)의 댓글 4300만개를 분석해 영상 6454개를 선정하고, 앤트로픽의 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'를 활용해 약 2시간 만에 서비스를 구축했다고 밝혔다.

현재 앤트로픽에 재직 중인 카르파시는 31일(현지시간) 자신의 블로그 를 통해 해커튜브를 소개하고, 이어 X를 통해 개발 과정과 주요 기능을 공개했다.

기존 유튜브의 추천 알고리즘 대신 기술 커뮤니티에서 공유된 영상과 이용자들의 평가를 기반으로 콘텐츠를 탐색하도록 설계했다.

개발 계기는 유튜브 이용 경험에 대한 불만이었다. 그는 30일 밤 유튜브에서 볼만한 영상을 찾다가 과장된 썸네일과 비슷한 주제의 반복적인 추천, 품질이 낮은 콘텐츠로 가득한 화면을 마주했다고 설명했다.

그는 "인터넷의 평균적인 이용자에게는 이 알고리즘이 잘 작동할지 모르지만, 적어도 나에게는 전혀 맞지 않는다"라고 밝혔다. 이어 다음 날 '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'에 해커뉴스에서 공유된 영상을 기반으로 유튜브와 비슷한 서비스를 만들어 달라고 요청했다.

해커튜브의 콘텐츠 데이터는 해커뉴스 댓글을 분석해 구축했다. 2007년부터 2026년까지 축적된 댓글 4300만개에서 유튜브 영상이 언급된 댓글 4만건을 추렸다. 이후 AI를 활용해 추천과 단순 언급, 비판 등을 구분하고 최종적으로 영상 6454개를 선정해 150개 주제로 분류했다.

영상 선정에는 최소 3명의 이용자가 서로 다른 3개월에 걸쳐 언급했는지 등을 고려했다. 이를 통해 특정 시점에만 화제가 된 콘텐츠보다 여러 시기에 반복적으로 공유된 영상을 찾아낼 수 있도록 했다. 데이터 정제 과정에는 '클로드 코드'의 워크플로우 기능과 '클로드 소네트' 모델을 활용했다.

해커튜브는 일반 유튜브와 달리 영상 제작자가 지정한 썸네일 대신 영상의 중간 지점에 해당하는 화면을 썸네일로 사용한다. 자극적인 이미지로 클릭을 유도하는 방식을 피하기 위한 설계다.

개인화 추천 기능도 제공한다. 별도 계정이나 서버에 개인정보를 저장하지 않고 브라우저에 이용 기록을 보관해 '포 유(For You)' 추천 콘텐츠를 구성한다. 사이트 데이터를 내보내 AI 에이전트에 전달하면 이용자가 자신만의 서비스를 만드는 데 활용할 수도 있다.

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5: https://t.co/xULTGY6VhH

— Andrej Karpathy (@karpathy) November 1, 2026

개발 과정에서 직접 코드를 작성하거나 터미널에서 명령어를 실행하지 않았다고 밝혔다. 맥용 클로드 코드 데스크톱 앱에서 오퍼스 5.5를 기본 모델로 설정하고 자연어로 작업을 지시하는 방식으로 프로젝트를 진행했다.

직접 수행한 작업은 유튜브 API 키 발급과 서버 준비, 도메인 구매 정도였다. 나머지 데이터 정리와 웹사이트 개발, 서버 배포, 보안 설정과 최적화는 클로드 코드에 맡겼다고 설명했다.

카르파시는 "더 이상 전통적인 엔지니어링이라고 할 만한 일을 하지 않는다"라며 "코드를 읽거나 쓰고 터미널에서 명령을 실행하는 대신 클로드와 대화하면서 모든 작업을 맡긴다"라고 말했다.

이번 프로젝트는 AI 코딩 에이전트가 코드 작성뿐 아니라 대규모 데이터 분석과 서비스 설계, 배포까지 수행할 수 있음을 보여주는 사례다. 그는 개발에 약 2시간이 걸렸다며 "이제 다시 숨을 쉴 수 있게 됐다"라고 밝혔다.

items.title: British businesses caught in Europe-wide supermarket fridge attacks
items.summary: Supermarket and grocery store refrigerator controls across Europe were hacked in the early hours of Monday in the second such wave of attacks in recent weeks — following a first wave in France — with unidentified perpetrators defrosting fridges and causing stock to spoil.
items.content:
Image: S. Laiba Ali via Unsplash British businesses caught in Europe-wide supermarket fridge attacks

Three meat suppliers in Britain are among businesses that have been caught in a wave of cyberattacks across Europe targeting refrigeration systems, according to an industry trade body.

Supermarket and grocery store refrigerator controls across Europe were hacked in the early hours of Monday in the second such wave of attacks in recent weeks — following a first wave in France — with unidentified perpetrators defrosting fridges and causing stock to spoil.

The Association of Independent Meat Suppliers (AIMS) told Recorded Future News that its three affected members were attacked through vulnerable Copeland XWEB supervisory controllers.

A Copeland spokesperson confirmed that certain XWEB monitoring solutions are impacted by the reported vulnerability. "We are continuing to assess the circumstances and have taken the appropriate actions based on the specific products involved," they said in a statement. "As part of our response, we have re-communicated the recommended patching and security protocols to ensure customers have the latest guidance to protect against the identified threats."

AIMS spokesperson Tony Goodger described the association’s members as “collateral” because they ran the same software. None of the affected members lost meat, he said, but the incident “must act as a reminder to all in the food industry, at whatever point in the supply chain they are, that their businesses may be seen by some as targets.”

No hackers have claimed responsibility for the attacks. British authorities say they have not attributed the incidents to any group, while a spokesperson for Belgium’s cybersecurity agency told Recorded Future News “it may never be possible to identify” who was behind them.

Langridge Organic, a British fruit and vegetable wholesaler, told trade publication The Grocer that it had also been attacked. The company’s managing director Alex Pearce said it "was amazing how many parameters" the attackers had changed after accessing the controllers.

Pearce said he was “pretty sure that I interrupted a live hacking event,” as he physically disconnected a fridge from the internet after observing it being remotely put into defrost mode. He said no stock was spoiled as a result of his team’s physical interventions.

All of the British suppliers were reportedly using vulnerable temperature controllers for which a firmware update had been available since August. According to a security note shared among AIMS members, firmware for Copeland XWEB — version 1.12.1 and earlier — contained “severe authentication bypass vulnerabilities that allow hackers to take control without a password.”

Britain’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said Tuesday it was aware of the refrigeration attacks and assisting affected organizations. Its staff had worked through the night in an attempt to proactively contact companies that it detected had vulnerable systems exposed to the internet.

Speaking at the launch of the agency’s annual report, Paul Chichester, its director of operations, said the impact was “minimal” so far.

Richard Horne, NCSC’s chief executive, added that “although at a national level the impact is minimal, if you’re running the business that’s been hit by that, it is an enormous issue for you and your employees and everyone else.”

The NCSC’s annual report raised the alarm about “the failure to implement even basic cyber protections” with Horne warning that Britain faced the “real prospect of an unprecedented rise in the number of cyber incidents” in the coming months.

The businesses impacted in the fridge attacks appear to fit that pattern, given that they were running firmware that was known to be flawed. In August, researchers at industrial cybersecurity company Claroty disclosed almost two dozen vulnerabilities in Copeland’s XWEB Pro controllers.

items.content:
딥시크가 자연어 지시만으로 AI 에이전트에 필요한 플러그인을 제작하는 '크리에이터 모드(Creator Mode)'를 공개했다. 사용자가 원하는 기능을 설명하면 AI가 코드를 작성하고 설치와 작동 검증까지 수행하는 방식으로, 복잡한 프로그래밍 지식 없이도 맞춤형 작업 도구를 만들 수 있다.

딥시크 하네스 팀은 2일 X를 통해 크리에이터 모드의 활용 사례를 소개하며 "아이디어를 직접 사용할 수 있는 플러그인으로 바꿀 수 있다"고 밝혔다. 이 기능은 앞서 개발된 것으로, 이번에 다양한 제작 사례와 활용 방법을 본격적으로 소개했다.

공개된 시연에서는 3D 모델을 렌더링하는 도구와 동영상 편집 작업 공간, 디자인 도구, 샌드박스 게임 등을 자연어 명령으로 제작했다. 동영상 편집 플러그인은 여러 영상을 불러와 타임라인에서 편집하고 결과물을 내보낼 수 있으며, 대화창에서 추가 편집을 요청하는 기능도 갖췄다.

논문을 읽으면서 특정 문장을 강조하거나 질문할 수 있는 도구와 토큰 사용량, 대화 횟수 등을 분석하는 플러그인도 선보였다. 딥시크는 시연에 사용한 7가지 프롬프트를 공개했으며, 일부 플러그인은 여러 차례 대화를 거쳐 완성했다고 설명했다.

크리에이터 모드는 단순히 코드를 생성하는 데 그치지 않는다. AI 에이전트가 필요한 개발 도구를 확인하고 플러그인 코드를 작성한 뒤 실행 환경에 설치하고 정상 작동 여부까지 점검한다. 공식 시연에서는 간단한 타이머 플러그인을 5분24초 만에 제작하고 설치와 검증까지 마쳤다.

Turn ideas into plugins that you can use, from a design workspace to a sandbox game or a 3D LLM visualizer.

What will you create? pic.twitter.com/MlXHIyyA1o

— DeepSeek Harness (@DeepSeekHarness) November 2, 2026

이 기능은 AI 에이전트 플랫폼 '딥시크 하네스(DeepSeek Harness)'를 기반으로 작동한다. 이용자가 직접 만든 플러그인을 연결하면 AI 에이전트의 기능과 작업 환경, 사용자 인터페이스를 확장할 수 있다.

딥시크는 최근 하네스를 중심으로 에이전트 개발 도구를 강화하고 있다. 지난 1일에는 여러 AI 에이전트의 작업을 관리하고 개발 과정을 자동화하는 코딩 '슈퍼 에이전트'를 공개했다.

크리에이터 모드는 여기에 이용자가 필요한 기능을 직접 제작하는 기능을 더한 것으로, 단순한 코딩 보조 도구를 넘어 확장 가능한 AI 작업 플랫폼을 구축하려는 시도로 볼 수 있다.

현재 하네스는 공식 웹사이트 에서 개발자 프리뷰 형태로 제공되며, 관련 소스코드도 오픈소스로 공개됐다.

다만 딥시크는 아직 보안 감사를 완료하지 않았다고 밝혔다. AI가 생성한 코드를 실행하고 외부 플러그인을 설치하는 구조여서 파일 수정이나 인증 정보 노출 등 보안 문제에 주의해야 한다.

items.title: 딥 프린시플, 일부 과학 평가서 GPT-6 아스트라 앞선 '하이드로젠' 공개
items.summary: 중국 AI 소재 연구 전문 딥 프린시플(Deep Principle)이 실제 실험 기록과 연구 과정의 시행착오까지 학습한 과학 특화 AI 모델 '하이드로젠-1.0(Hydrogen-1.0)'을 공개했다. 총 7530억개 매개변수를 갖춘 오픈웨이트 모델로, 과학적 지식과 추론 능력을 넘어 실험 설계와 시뮬레이션, 신소재 탐색 등 여러 단계의 연구 작업을 수행하도록 설계했다.딥 프린시플은 2일(현지시간) 하이드로젠-1.0을 공개하고 모델 가중치를 MIT 라이선스로 허깅페이스와 모델스코프에 배포했다.Z.a
items.content:
중국 AI 소재 연구 전문 딥 프린시플(Deep Principle)이 실제 실험 기록과 연구 과정의 시행착오까지 학습한 과학 특화 AI 모델 '하이드로젠-1.0(Hydrogen-1.0)'을 공개했다. 총 7530억개 매개변수를 갖춘 오픈웨이트 모델로, 과학적 지식과 추론 능력을 넘어 실험 설계와 시뮬레이션, 신소재 탐색 등 여러 단계의 연구 작업을 수행하도록 설계했다.

딥 프린시플은 2일(현지시간) 하이드로젠-1.0 을 공개하고 모델 가중치를 MIT 라이선스로 허깅페이스 와 모델스코프 에 배포했다.

Z.ai의 범용 모델 'GLM-5.3'을 기반으로 과학 분야 전문 지식과 자체 연구소의 실험 기록 등을 추가 학습했다. 전문가 혼합(MoE) 구조를 적용해 토큰당 약 400억개 매개변수만 활성화하며, 최대 100만 토큰의 문맥을 지원한다.

성능 평가에서는 일부 과학 연구 과제에서 최첨단 독점 모델을 앞섰다. 딥 프린시플 자체 평가에 따르면 과학 연구 역량을 측정하는 '프론티어사이언스-리서치(FrontierScience-Research·FSR)'에서 하이드로젠-1.0은 38.3%를 기록해 'GPT-6 아스트라'의 33.3%보다 5%포인트 높은 점수를 얻었다.

대학원 수준의 과학 지식을 평가하는 'GPQA 다이아몬드'에서도 기반 모델인 GLM-5.3보다 높은 성능을 보였으며, 오픈 모델인 '키미-K3'와 비슷한 수준을 기록했다.

실제 연구 환경을 반영한 내부 평가에서는 과학 컴퓨팅과 화학 반응 예측에서 GPT-6 아스트라를 각각 5.13%p, 4.76%p 앞섰다. 다만 핵자기공명(NMR)을 이용한 분자 구조 규명에서는 GPT-6 아스트라가 3.33%p 높은 점수를 기록했다.

이번 모델의 가장 큰 특징은 실제 연구 과정에서 축적한 성공과 실패의 기록을 학습했다는 점이다. 딥 프린시플은 화학·재료과학·생명과학 분야의 전문 지식과 연구진의 피드백, 전자연구노트(ELN), AI 에이전트의 연구 수행 기록을 활용했다.

특히 자체 연구 플랫폼 '미라(Mira)'를 통해 실험 목적과 절차, 관찰 결과, 후속 연구 방향을 연결한 데이터를 확보했다. 성공한 실험뿐 아니라 실패한 시도와 예상하지 못한 결과도 포함했다. 이를 통해 모델이 단순히 과학 문제의 정답을 찾는 데 그치지 않고, 실험 결과에 따라 다음 연구 방향을 결정하거나 잘못된 접근법을 수정하도록 학습시켰다. 지도 미세조정(SFT)과 강화학습(RL)을 결합해 연구 수행 능력을 높였다.

실제 시연에서도 여러 단계의 연구 작업을 수행했다. 재료과학 분야에서는 폴리에틸렌의 분자 구조를 구성하는 파이썬 코드를 작성하고 분자 동역학 시뮬레이션 도구인 GROMACS를 실행했다. 실행 과정에서 발생한 오류를 스스로 발견해 수정한 뒤 시뮬레이션을 다시 진행하고, 결과를 바탕으로 물질의 밀도와 분자 배열, 확산 특성 등을 분석했다.

실험실 자동화 작업에서는 12개 바이알을 이용하는 스즈키 커플링 화학 실험의 실행 절차를 생성했다. 가상 실험 환경에서 피펫 팁을 장착하지 않은 채 액체를 흡입하려는 오류를 발견하자 작업 순서를 수정해 검증을 마쳤다. 다만 실제 실험 장비를 작동한 것이 아니라 가상 환경에서 절차의 실행 가능성을 확인한 사례다.

신소재 탐색에서도 성과를 보였다. 전이금속 착물의 전자 에너지 차이를 최대화하는 과제에서 5차례에 걸쳐 후보 물질을 제안하고 평가 결과에 따라 탐색 방향을 수정했다. 최종 후보의 평균 에너지 차이는 4.318전자볼트(eV)로, GPT-6 아스트라의 3.689eV와 키미-K3의 3.353eV를 앞섰다. 딥 프린시플은 제한된 탐색 횟수 안에 연구 목표에 부합하는 후보 물질을 찾아내는 능력을 보여줬다고 설명했다. 다만 실제 새로운 물질의 합성이나 실험적 검증을 완료한 것은 아니다.

이번 공개는 과학 연구용 AI를 오픈웨이트로 제공한다는 점에서도 의미가 있다. 최근 오픈AI와 앤트로픽이 AI를 활용한 수학·생명과학 연구 성과를 발표했지만, 주요 모델은 독점적으로 운영하고 있다. 딥 프린시플은 연구자들이 모델을 직접 실행하고 수정할 수 있도록 가중치를 공개했다. 다만 전체 학습 데이터와 구체적인 학습 과정까지 공개한 것은 아니다.

실행 환경은 엔비디아와 AMD GPU를 모두 지원하며, 8개 GPU 구성에서 추론을 검증했다. SGLang을 이용해 오픈AI 호환 API 형태로도 실행할 수 있다.
